The main takeaway from our work is that
low-intensity continuous improvement interventions are not likely to be effective in improving secondary prevention medication use after cardiac surgery.

continuous quality improvement interventions, which are low intensity, low cost, and low effort, are effective for increasing secondary prevention adherence after cardiac surgery, and they may be effective in other settings as well.
